mainTopic: Whose קרבן פסח a person eats from when two people slaughtered for him, and the אגדה that follows on שיר השירים, תהלים and the prophet הושע
overview: The משנה lists cases where two different people slaughtered a קרבן פסח for the same person. A married woman eats from her husband's. On the first רגל, at her father's house, she may choose. An orphan may choose between his guardians, but a slave of two partners eats from neither, and a half-slave does not eat from his master's. The גמרא asks whether the woman's choice proves ברירה, and answers no, because she chose by the time of the שחיטה. A ברייתא seems to contradict the משנה, and the גמרא answers that it depends on whether the bride is eager to go to her father's house. This leads to אגדה on פסוקים from שיר השירים and תהלים praising Torah scholars and the pure youth of ישראל. Then the גמרא turns to ספר הושע: הושע was the first of four prophets in his era. When he suggested replacing ישראל, ה׳ had him marry גמר to teach him that one never sends away one's own family. The explanation of her name continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A married woman eats from her husband's פסח
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens: a woman living in her husband's house, for whom both husband and father slaughtered a קרבן פסח, eats from her husband's.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A woman who is living in her husband's house, if her husband slaughtered a פסח for her and her father also slaughtered one for her, she eats from her husband's.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic case. A married woman living with her husband is counted with her husband's group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To eat from a קרבן פסח, a person must be registered (מנוי) on it before it is slaughtered. Here two people tried to register her. We assume a woman settled in her husband's home wants to be with her husband, so her registration goes to his group.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtered (the קרבן פסח) on her behalf, registering her

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman
when she is in her husband's house,
if her husband slaughtered on her behalf
and her father slaughtered on her behalf —
she eats from her husband's.
phrases.notes: We assume her intent is to be with her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה בִּזְמַן שֶׁהִיא בְּבֵית בַּעְלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman living in her husband's home eats from her husband's קרבן פסח when both husband and father slaughtered for her.

steps.title: First festival at her father's house: she may choose
steps.stepSummary: If she went to her father's house for the first רגל after marriage, and both slaughtered for her, she eats wherever she wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she went for the first festival to spend it at her father's house, and her father slaughtered for her and her husband slaughtered for her, she eats in whichever place she wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case where the woman is at her father's house for the first רגל. Here she may choose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It was customary for a new bride to spend the first רגל at her father's home. In that situation we cannot assume she wants her husband's group, so her own choice decides. This phrase 'בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהִיא רוֹצָה' is what the גמרא will analyze below.

keyTerms.meaning: The first pilgrimage festival after her marriage

steps.whyThisMatters: The words 'wherever she wants' set up the גמרא's question about ברירה, and the whole case sets up the contradiction from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: If she went for the first festival
to spend it in her father's house,
and her father slaughtered on her behalf
and her husband slaughtered on her behalf —
she eats in whichever place she wants.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלְכָה רֶגֶל רִאשׁוֹן לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּבֵית אָבִיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasting case to step 1: same woman, but at her father's house for the first רגל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first רגל at her father's house, she may eat from whichever פסח she chooses.

steps.title: An orphan with several guardians may choose
steps.stepSummary: If an orphan's guardians each slaughtered for him, he eats wherever he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: An orphan whose guardians slaughtered on his behalf eats in whichever place he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case: an orphan with more than one guardian. He may choose whose פסח to eat from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No guardian has a stronger claim on the orphan than another. So, like the woman on the first רגל, his own choice decides.

keyTerms.meaning: Guardians appointed to manage an orphan's affairs

phrases.english: An orphan whose guardians slaughtered on his behalf —
he eats in whichever place he wants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case to step 2, where the person chooses
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An orphan with multiple guardians who each slaughtered for him may eat from whichever he chooses.

steps.title: A slave of two partners eats from neither
steps.stepSummary: A slave owned jointly by two partners may not eat from either partner's פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A slave of two partners may not eat from the פסח of either of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the person may not choose. A jointly owned slave cannot eat from either owner's פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave does not decide for himself. Each partner owns only half of him, so neither partner's registration fully covers him. Unless they agreed in advance, he eats from neither.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the orphan. The orphan may choose, but the slave cannot choose and so eats from neither.

phrases.english: A slave of two partners
may not eat from that of either of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasting case: here there is no free choice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave owned by two partners eats from neither partner's פסח.

steps.title: A half-slave does not eat from his master's פסח
steps.stepSummary: One who is half slave and half free may not eat from his master's פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who is half slave and half free man may not eat from his master's פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a person who is half slave and half free. He cannot eat from his master's פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The master owns only the slave half. We assume the master did not intend to include the free half, so the person is not fully registered on the master's פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Half slave and half free man

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה: a married woman goes with her husband; on the first רגל at her father's house she chooses; an orphan chooses; a slave of partners eats from neither; a half-slave does not eat from his master's.

phrases.english: One who is half slave
and half free man
may not eat from his master's.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the משנה, continuing the slave cases
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who is half slave and half free does not eat from his master's פסח.

steps.title: Does the woman's choice prove retroactive clarification?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether 'she eats wherever she wants' proves that there is ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Can you learn from this that there is retroactive clarification?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by suggesting a big conclusion from the משנה: that ברירה works. This is setting up the next step, which will reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person must be registered on a פסח before the שחיטה. If she chooses only later, then her later choice must 'reveal' that she was registered there all along. That is the idea of ברירה, a debated principle, so the גמרא is surprised the משנה would decide it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
There is retroactive clarification: a later choice shows what was true from the start

phrases.english: GEMARA: Can you learn from it
that there is retroactive clarification?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the phrase 'בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהִיא רוֹצָה' from the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the woman's (and orphan's) later choice shows that the משנה holds יש ברירה.

steps.title: No proof: she chose at the time of slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: 'she wants' means she chose already at the time of שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'she wants' mean? At the time of slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own suggestion. The choice was made by the time of the שחיטה, so there is no proof for ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her choice was already made when the animal was slaughtered, she was clearly registered in one group from the start. Nothing needs to be clarified 'backwards,' so ברירה is not involved at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove ברירה, because the choice happens by the time of שחיטה.

phrases.english: What does 'she wants' mean? —
At the time of slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof for יש ברירה from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the choice came after the שחיטה; really it was made by the time of שחיטה, so nothing is clarified retroactively.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to contradict the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: on the first רגל she eats from her father's; after that she may choose father or husband. This clashes with the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction: A woman, on the first festival, eats from her father's. From then on, if she wants she eats from her father's, and if she wants, from her husband's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets one source against another. The ברייתא's rules seem to conflict with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says on the first רגל she chooses, and normally (at home) she eats from her husband's. The ברייתא says the opposite: on the first רגל she eats from her father's, and only afterward may she choose. The גמרא will need to resolve this clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (between two sources)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two clashes here: about the first רגל (choice vs. father's) and about later festivals (husband's vs. choice). Keep both in mind.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: A woman,
on the first festival eats from her father's.
From here on,
if she wants — she eats from her father's,
if she wants — from her husband's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the woman's case in the משנה and challenges it from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rulings about the married woman (steps 1 and 2)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives her father's פסח on the first רגל and a free choice afterward, while the משנה gives a choice on the first רגל and her husband's otherwise.

steps.title: It depends on whether she is eager to go to her father's house
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא (she may eat from her father's) speaks of a woman eager to visit her father's house. The משנה (she eats from her husband's) speaks of a woman who is not eager.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, she is eager to go. There, she is not eager.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between the משנה and the ברייתא. It says they are talking about two different kinds of women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some brides still feel a strong pull to their father's home, so we assume they want to be counted in their father's group. That is the ברייתא. A bride who does not feel that pull is assumed to want her husband's group, and that is the משנה, so there is really no argument.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This is a formula that opens an answer.
Here... there. The two sources refer to different cases.
Eager, as if being chased, to go (to her father's house)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and the ברייתא do not argue. Where she eats depends on her emotional pull toward her father's home.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not decide the question of ברירה. It only explains which group a woman is assumed to want to be counted in.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, it refers to one who is eager to go (to her father's house).
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא, where she may eat from her father's.

phrases.english: There, it refers to one who is not eager.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה, where she eats from her husband's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source speaks of a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא seemed to give opposite rulings about the same woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to a bride eager to go to her father's house. The משנה refers to one who is not eager.

steps.title: A verse showing that a new bride is eager to go to her father's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains 'as one who finds peace' as a bride who was welcomed in her father-in-law's house and hurries to tell her father's family about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written, 'Then I was in his eyes as one who finds peace.' And רבי יוחנן said: like a bride found perfect in her father-in-law's house, who is eager to go and tell her praise in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק and רבי יוחנן's explanation to show that a bride really can feel eager to go back to her father's home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This supports the idea of 'רדופה לילך' from the previous step. A happy bride wants to run home and share her good news, so her strong tie to her father's house is realistic.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who finds peace (שיר השירים ח:י)
Her father-in-law's house, meaning her husband's family home

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Then I was in his eyes as one who finds peace,'
And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Like a bride who was found perfect in her father-in-law's house,
and is eager to go
to tell of her praise in her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives scriptural support for the 'eager bride' case in Step 9
steps.raayaObject: That a new bride can be eager to go to her father's house
steps.raayaSupportSource: שיר השירים ח:י as explained by רבי יוחנן

steps.title: A second verse comparing a bride in her father-in-law's house and in her father's house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains 'You shall call Me my husband, not my master' as the closeness of a bride living in her husband's home, not a bride still living in her father's home.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And it shall be on that day, says ה׳, you will call Me my husband, and no longer call Me my master.' רבי יוחנן said: like a bride in her father-in-law's house, and not like a bride in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק with רבי יוחנן's explanation. It contrasts a bride who lives with her husband with a bride still in her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the phrases 'בית חמיה' and 'בית אביה' mark two different stages of a bride's life. While she is in her father's house her bond with her husband is still distant. In her father-in-law's house it is close, like 'אישי'.

keyTerms.meaning: My husband. This expresses closeness and love.
My master. This expresses a more formal, distant relationship.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And it shall be on that day, says ה׳,'
you shall call Me: My Husband,
and you shall no longer call Me: My Master,'
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Like a bride in her father-in-law's house,
and not like a bride in her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק that uses the same bride imagery
steps.raayaObject: The difference between a bride at her father's house and a bride at her father-in-law's house
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע ב:יח as explained by רבי יוחנן

steps.title: The little sister with no breasts: עילם learned but did not teach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains 'We have a little sister, and she has no breasts' as the community of עילם, which merited to learn Torah but not to teach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We have a little sister, and she has no breasts.' רבי יוחנן said: this is עילם, which merited to learn but did not merit to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted שיר השירים, it moves into אגדה on a nearby פסוק. This is a new side topic, not part of the הלכה of קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breasts are a picture of giving nourishment to others. A 'sister with no breasts' is a community that gained Torah for itself but could not pass it on to others.

keyTerms.meaning: עילם, a region and its Jewish community

phrases.english: 'We have a little sister,'
'and she has no breasts,'
Rabbi Yochanan said: This is Eilam,
which merited to learn,
but did not merit to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side topic triggered by the שיר השירים verse quoted in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עילם learned Torah but did not spread it to others.

steps.title: 'I am a wall' means the Torah, and the towers are Torah scholars
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains 'I am a wall' as the Torah and 'my breasts are like towers' as תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers.' רבי יוחנן said: 'I am a wall' is the Torah. 'My breasts are like towers' are the Torah scholars.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the אגדה with another פסוק from שיר השירים, which is the same verse quoted in Step 10. Here it brings רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah protects like a wall. The תלמידי חכמים are like towers on that wall: they 'nurse' and guard the people by teaching Torah to them. This is the opposite of עילם in Step 12.

phrases.english: 'I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers,'
Rabbi Yochanan said:
'I am a wall': this is the Torah;
'and my breasts are like towers': these are the Torah scholars.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֲנִי חוֹמָה וְשָׁדַי כַּמִּגְדָּלוֹת״, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the aggadic chain on שיר השירים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wall is the Torah, and the towers are the תלמידי חכמים who spread it.

steps.title: רבא's reading: the wall is the Jewish people, and the towers are shuls and study halls
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains 'I am a wall' as כנסת ישראל and 'my breasts are like towers' as בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: 'I am a wall' is the Congregation of Israel. 'My breasts are like towers' are the synagogues and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different explanation of the same פסוק, this time from רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, the wall is the Jewish people as a whole. The 'towers' that nourish them are the places of prayer and Torah study. רבי יוחנן focused on the Torah and the scholars, while רבא focuses on the nation and its institutions.

keyTerms.meaning: The Congregation of Israel, meaning the Jewish people as a whole

steps.whatToRemember: The halachic answer is that the משנה and the ברייתא do not argue: it depends on whether the bride is eager to go to her father's house. The אגדה that follows teaches that Torah must be both learned and spread, through scholars (רבי יוחנן) or through shuls and study halls (רבא).

phrases.english: And Rava said:
'I am a wall': this is the Congregation of Israel;
'and my breasts are like towers':
these are the synagogues and study halls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative reading of the same verse explained by רבי יוחנן in Step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wall is כנסת ישראל, and the towers are בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

steps.title: רב quotes a verse about sons like plants and daughters like corners
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא בר טוביה, quoting רב, introduces the verse in תהלים 144:12 that he is about to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: What is the meaning of the verse, 'We whose sons are like plants grown up in their youth, whose daughters are like corner pillars carved in the shape of a palace'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב quotes a verse and asks what it means, getting ready to explain it phrase by phrase in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the theme of the earlier steps: דרשות that praise כלל ישראל. The question 'מאי דכתיב' means 'what is this verse really teaching?' It does not mean the verse is difficult.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (an opening for a דרשה)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב,
phrases.english: Rav Zutra bar Toviya said that Rav said
What is meant by that which is written
"We whose sons are like plants
grown up in their youth
whose daughters are like corner pillars carved
in the shape of a palace"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another דרשה in praise of Israel, following the דרשות of רבי יוחנן and רבא.

steps.title: Sons like plants are young men who never sinned
steps.stepSummary: 'Sons like plants' refers to Jewish young men who never tasted sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We whose sons are like plants' — these are the young men of Israel who have never tasted the taste of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the first phrase. The 'plants' are pure young men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A young sapling that grows well is healthy and has no damage. In the same way, these young men grew up whole and were never damaged by sin.

phrases.english: "We whose sons are like plants"
these are the young men of Israel
who have not tasted the taste of sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first phrase of the verse quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Plants' are young men untouched by sin.

steps.title: Daughters like corners are young women faithful to their future husbands
steps.stepSummary: 'Daughters like corners' refers to Jewish young women who keep themselves sealed only for their husbands.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Whose daughters are like corner pillars' — these are the young women of Israel who keep themselves closed off, saving themselves only for their husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the second phrase. The 'corners' are modest young women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a 'corner' is something full and closed. These young women stay closed to everyone except the man they will marry. The next two steps bring verses to prove that 'corner' means something full.

keyTerms.meaning: The young unmarried women of Israel
Their openings (a modest way of describing their bodies)

phrases.english: "Whose daughters are like corner pillars"
these are the young women of Israel
who keep their openings closed, saving them for their husbands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second phrase of the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Corners' are young women who stay sealed for their husbands.

steps.title: Proof from זכריה that corners are filled
steps.stepSummary: A verse in זכריה shows that the 'corners of the altar' are something filled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so the verse says: 'They shall be filled like the basins, like the corners of the altar.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that the word 'corner' is connected with being full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In זכריה, the corners of the מזבח are described as 'filled.' This supports reading 'corners' in תהלים as full and sealed, the way the young women are.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (brings a supporting verse)
A basin used for the blood of קרבנות

phrases.english: And similarly it says:
"And they shall be filled like the basins
like the corners of the altar"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the reading of 'corners' given in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That 'זויות' means something full and sealed.

steps.title: Second proof from the next verse in תהלים
steps.stepSummary: Another option: the very next verse in תהלים calls 'our corners' full.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you prefer, learn it from here: 'Our corners are full, providing every kind of food.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second proof for the same point, from the verse right after the one being explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איבעית אימא' gives a different source that proves the same idea. It does not argue with the first proof. Because this verse is from the same passage in תהלים, it is an especially close support.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (offers another option)
From kind to kind, every type

phrases.english: If you wish, say it from here:
"Our corners are full
providing every kind of food"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative proof for the same point as step 18.

steps.title: Both groups count as if the Temple was built in their days
steps.stepSummary: 'Carved in the shape of a palace' teaches that the pure young men and women are credited as if the בית המקדש was built in their time.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Carved in the shape of a palace' — the verse credits both of these groups as if the Sanctuary were built in their days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the last phrase of the verse. It completes the דרשה by showing how great these young people are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'היכל' links the youth to the בית המקדש. Living a pure and modest life is treated as great as having the בית המקדש built in one's lifetime. 'אלו ואלו' means the reward applies to both the young men and the young women.
steps.whatToRemember: Pure young men (never tasted sin) and modest young women (faithful to their future husbands) are credited as if the בית המקדש was built in their days.

phrases.english: "Carved in the shape of a palace"
the verse credits both these and those
as if the Sanctuary were built in their days.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מְחֻטָּבוֹת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל״ — אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ מַעֲלֶה עֲלֵיהֶן הַכָּתוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the verse after the proofs and explains its final phrase.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The pure youth of Israel are credited as if the היכל was built in their days.

steps.title: Four prophets in one era, and הושע was the eldest
steps.stepSummary: Starting from the first verse of הושע, the גמרא says four prophets prophesied in one era, and הושע was the greatest of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The word of ה׳ that came to הושע, in the days of עוזיהו, יותם, אחז and יחזקיה, kings of יהודה.' Four prophets prophesied in one era, and the greatest of them was הושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: the opening verse of ספר הושע. It says four prophets lived in the same period and names הושע as the greatest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse lists four kings, which points to one historical era. Here 'גדול' means the senior one, who came first. That is why the proof in the next step uses the word 'תחלת' (at first).

keyTerms.meaning: One period of time, one era
The greatest (or oldest) of them all

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'פרק' does not mean a chapter of a book. It means a period of time.

phrases.aramaic: ״דְּבַר ה׳ אֲשֶׁר הָיָה אֶל הוֹשֵׁעַ וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: "The word of ה׳ that came to Hoshea, etc.
in the days of Uzziah, Yotham, Achaz, Chizkiyah
kings of Yehudah".
Four prophets prophesied in one era,
and the greatest of them all was Hoshea,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new aggadic topic in ספר הושע, connected to the earlier use of verses from הושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four prophets prophesied in one era, and הושע was the greatest.

steps.title: Proof that הושע came first
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'At first ה׳ spoke with Hoshea' proves that הושע was first among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'At first ה׳ spoke with הושע.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a verse to prove that הושע was the leading prophet of that era.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'תחלת' (at first) shows that הושע came before the others. But read literally, the verse seems to call him the first prophet ever, and the next step will challenge that.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a proof-verse)

phrases.english: as it says: "At first ה׳ spoke with Hoshea."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That הושע was the greatest or first of the four prophets.

steps.title: But many prophets came before הושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the verse: how can הושע be 'first' when many prophets lived between משה and הושע?
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it really with הושע that ה׳ spoke first? Weren't there many prophets from משה until הושע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the simple reading of 'תחלת.' History shows that הושע was not the first prophet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'first' means first of all prophets, the verse would contradict the fact that there were many earlier prophets, starting with משה. So the word must mean something narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: And is it really so? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Was it really with Hoshea that He spoke first?
Weren't there, from Moshe until Hoshea,
many prophets!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal reading of the proof-verse in step 22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many prophets came before הושע, so he cannot be the first prophet ever.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: first among the four prophets of that era
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that הושע was first only among the four prophets of that era: הושע, ישעיה, עמוס and מיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He was first of the four prophets who prophesied in that era. They are הושע, ישעיה, עמוס and מיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן resolves the challenge by limiting 'first' to the group of four prophets from that period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse does not mean first of all prophets in history. It means first among his contemporaries. This also tells us who the four prophets of step 21 were.
steps.whatToRemember: הושע was the first and greatest of the four prophets of one era: הושע, ישעיה, עמוס and מיכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
He was first of the four prophets
who prophesied in that era,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: הוֹשֵׁעַ, יְשַׁעְיָה, עָמוֹס וּמִיכָה.
phrases.english: and they are: Hoshea, Yeshayah, Amos and Michah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: תְּחִלָּה לְאַרְבָּעָה נְבִיאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תחלת' means first of all prophets ever.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תחלת' means first among the four prophets of that era.

steps.title: ה׳ tells הושע that his children have sinned
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא tells הושע that the Jewish people have sinned. The גמרא says הושע should have answered by asking for mercy on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to הושע: Your children have sinned. הושע should have said: They are Your children, the children of the people You love, the children of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. Pour Your mercy on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about הושע. It describes what ה׳ told him and what the right answer would have been.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ calls the Jewish people 'your children', meaning הושע's people. The proper answer was to turn it around and say they are ה׳'s children and descendants of the אבות, which is a reason for mercy. This sets up the failure in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: ה׳ said 'your children' as a test. The right answer was to say 'no, they are Your children', not to agree that they belong only to הושע.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהוֹשֵׁעַ:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Hoshea:
Your children have sinned.
He should have said:
They are Your children, they are the children of Your beloved ones,
the children of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,
pour Your mercy over them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהוֹשֵׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After identifying הושע as the first of the four prophets, the גמרא tells the story behind his first prophecy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When told that ישראל sinned, a prophet should plead for mercy because they are ה׳'s children and children of the אבות.

steps.title: הושע suggests replacing the Jewish people
steps.stepSummary: Instead of pleading for mercy, הושע told ה׳ that the whole world is His and He should swap ישראל for another nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not only did he not say that, he even said before Him: Master of the World, the whole world is Yours. Exchange them for a different nation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what הושע actually said. He did not defend the Jewish people and even suggested replacing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'not only' shows two levels of failure: he did not defend them, and he also suggested giving them up. This answer is what leads ה׳ to teach him a lesson in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that / it was not enough for him

phrases.english: Not only did he not say this,
but he said before Him:
Master of the World,
the whole world is Yours,
exchange them for another nation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts what הושע should have said (step 25) with what he actually said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הושע failed to defend ישראל and suggested replacing them with another nation.

steps.title: ה׳'s plan to teach הושע a lesson
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ plans to have הושע marry a זונה and have children, then tell him to send her away. If he can, ה׳ will send away ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said: What shall I do with this old man? I will tell him: Go and take a זונה and have children of זנות. Afterwards I will tell him: Send her away from you. If he is able to send her away, I too will send away ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes ה׳'s plan to show הושע why He cannot give up on the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson works through feeling: even a wife of bad character and children of doubtful origin become hard to send away once they are your family. If הושע cannot do it, he will understand that ה׳ will never abandon ישראל, His own children.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main lesson of the story: ה׳'s bond with ישראל is like family, and family is not replaced even when they do wrong.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
What shall I do with this elder?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמַר לוֹ: לֵךְ וְקַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה
phrases.english: I will say to him: Go and take a prostitute
and have children of prostitution for yourself,
and afterward I will say to him:
Send her away from before you.
If he is able to send her away,
I too will send away Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה לְזָקֵן זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ה׳ responds to הושע's suggestion from step 26 by planning a lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ will teach הושע through his own family that one cannot send away one's own, just as ה׳ will not send away ישראל.

steps.title: The verses in הושע that show this plan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוקים in which ה׳ tells הושע to marry a זונה, and הושע marries גמר בת דבלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'ה׳ said to הושע: Go, take for yourself a wife of זנות and children of זנות.' And it is written: 'He went and took גמר בת דבלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the story from the actual פסוקים at the start of ספר הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows ה׳ commanding the marriage, which matches the plan in step 27. The second פסוק shows הושע carrying it out and gives the wife's name, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
Gomer the daughter of Divlayim, הושע's wife

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'ה׳ said to Hoshea:

phrases.aramaic: לֵךְ קַח לְךָ אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים וְיַלְדֵי זְנוּנִים״,
phrases.english: Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution,'
And it is written: 'So he went and took
Gomer the daughter of Divlayim.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the story of step 27 with the פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: That ה׳ commanded הושע to marry a זונה as part of His plan.

steps.title: רב explains the name גמר
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that she was called גמר because everyone would finish their desires with her. The גמרא then begins explaining 'בת דבלים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'גמר': רב said, because everyone would finish (satisfy themselves) with her. 'The daughter of...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the wife's name as a hint to her immoral behavior. Then it starts explaining the second part of her name, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the name גמר as related to the word גומרים, 'finish'. This fits the פסוק's description of her as an אשת זנונים. The word 'בת' opens the next explanation, of 'בת דבלים'.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא רב, who gives this explanation

steps.confusionAlert: The word 'בת' at the end is not a complete thought. It is the start of the next explanation, about 'בת דבלים', which continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: 'Gomer': Rav said:
because everyone would finish with her.
'The daughter of…'
phrases.notes: Begins the explanation of 'בת דבלים', which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֹּמֶר אָמַר רַב שֶׁהַכֹּל גּוֹמְרִים בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the name גמר from the פסוק quoted in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name גמר hints that everyone finished their desires with her, matching her description as an אשת זנונים.
